STATUS: fail
SUMMARY: Two reproduced blocking failures: the Dialog focus trap leaks after a backdrop click (focus goes to body, and the first Tab lands on a button behind the modal), and Combobox clears the value on Enter or blur with empty text, which contradicts C5 and C8. Tabs, the Dialog Escape and nesting logic, and the G2 passthrough all held up under probing. The probe files are deleted and `git status` matches the starting state.

FILES TOUCHED: none (scratch probes were created in tests/ as `__probe_*.test.tsx` and deleted)

FINDINGS:
- [blocking] D3 focus trap leak. Clicking the backdrop moves focus to `BODY`. The next Tab then goes to the page behind the dialog. `trapTab` only runs when the keydown target is inside the dialog, so it never fires. Repro: render `<><button>outside</button><Dialog open onOpenChange={()>{}} title="T"><button>one</button><button>two</button></Dialog></>`, then `user.click(backdrop)`, then `user.tab()`. Result: `activeElement` is `outside`. Expected: focus stays inside the dialog.
- [blocking] C5/C8 conflict. Enter with an empty text box calls `onChange(null)`, and blur with empty text does the same. C5 says "Enter with no active option does nothing", and C8 says blur "restores the text to the selected label". Repro with `defaultValue="apple"`: `user.click(input); user.clear(input); user.keyboard("{Enter}")` gives `onChange` calls `[[null]]`. `user.clear(input); user.tab()` gives `onChange` `[[null]]` and text `""` (expected `"Apple"`). The README documents this behaviour (lines 127, 138–144), so the README and the acceptance criteria disagree. The orchestrator needs to decide which one wins.
- [minor] Tabs: a tab's `aria-controls` points at a panel id that does not exist when no matching `TabPanel` is rendered. Not reproduced as a failure; it is a checklist concern about dangling ids.
- [minor] Tabs: duplicate `value`s produce duplicate ids. Not probed beyond a no-crash check.
- [minor] Tabs: removing the selected tab leaves the stale `internal` value, so re-adding that value re-selects it. Not reproduced.
- [minor] Combobox: `onChange` fires even when re-selecting the current option. C1 does not require otherwise. Not reproduced as a bug.

CHECKS:
- `pnpm vitest run` on a combobox probe set (C2, C4, C5, C6, C8, C9): C6 Escape restores the label and removes `aria-activedescendant` → pass. C4 ArrowDown wraps and skips disabled options → pass (my first assertion was wrong; the code is right). C5 Enter on empty text → FAIL (blocking above). C8 blur on empty text → FAIL (blocking above). C9 regex-like typing was not exercised: user-event rejects `[` as a key descriptor, so it needs `fireEvent.change`, which I did not run. C2 listbox name was not exercised: the listbox is hidden until opened, and my probe clicked without opening it, so it is inconclusive.
- Tabs probes (T1 controlled-ignore and reselect, T2 ids with spaces and slashes and two instances, T3 Tab-in and Tab-to-panel, T4/T5 Home/End with first and last disabled, a single enabled tab, StrictMode double registration with wrap, removing the selected tab, empty-string value) → all pass.
- Dialog probes (D1 no `aria-describedby` without description, `className` and data passthrough, D2 focus on open, D3 no-focusable Tab keeps focus, D4 drag from content to backdrop does not close and backdrop click does, D5 focus restored after controlled Escape close, D6 nested dialogs close only the top one, D6 Combobox Escape closes the popup and the dialog stays open) → all pass, except the D3 backdrop leak above.
- G2 passthrough probe: `className`, user `onKeyDown`/`onClick`/`onBlur` are called, and the ARIA attributes still hold → pass.
- Not run: `pnpm test` and `pnpm typecheck` (the orchestrator already ran them). The README's Combobox table and the Escape row were checked only against the code, not via a probe.

OPEN QUESTIONS:
- Should Enter or blur with empty text clear the value to `null` (as the README documents), or should it follow C5/C8 (do nothing, and restore the selected label)? This decides the two blocking findings above.
